title: The one and zero fibre squares of the canonical section comparisons
statement: For every finite purity datum P [def-pur-conventions], the actual family restriction of an etale map of smooth section pairs [def-pur-section-restriction-data] restricts at one to the original restriction and at zero to the induced normal restriction, through endpointOne and endpointZero. Under any Cartesian base change over separated finite-type k-schemes, endpointOne and endpointZero commute with the family and endpoint baseComparison maps through the specified endpointPull constraint. This statement asserts the four endpoint squares; it asserts no equation involving the normalized delta map.

proof.text: Construct the one- and zero-fibre BaseChange structures from the actual Rees fibre pullback squares. The endpointOne and endpointZero formulas are definitionally the corresponding baseComparison maps, including all finite-site comparison factors.

Apply the restriction-naturality clause of section_base_comparison_laws to the family etale map along the one section, with the original etale map as its fibre. Apply it along the zero section with normalEtaleMap as its fibre. The two upper-map commutations are exactly the endpoint equations in geometry. This proves both restriction squares.

For a commuting rectangle of four base-change squares, the two composite BaseChange structures have the same upper map. Transport along equality of the two composite base maps identifies their baseComparison maps. Expand both using the BasePasting clause of section_base_comparison_laws and cancel the first pullback compositor. This gives the rectangle equation with the inverse compositor, morphism-equality comparison, and second compositor in precisely the endpointPull order.

Apply the rectangle equation to familyBaseChange and the two one-fibre squares, using reesBaseGeometry for the upper-map equality. Apply it again to the two zero-fibre squares and normalBaseChange; its upper-map equality is the first projection equation of the defining normalBaseMap pullback lift. These are the two required endpoint base-change equations. No flatness, positive dimension, orientation, or nonemptiness assumption enters.
